tasks.short: Help site managers cost their plans, allocate shared costs and prepare budgets.

today.trigger: A site manager requests costing advice, or the budget and forecast cycle opens.
steps: Pull actual costs, payroll totals and current budgets from AFAS and the nightly extract.
Collect assumptions from Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, including agency rates and shift requirements.
Calculate costs and allocate shared expenses in Excel using agreed allocation keys.
Discuss assumptions with managers and explain the financial implications.
Revise the budget and submit advice to the Controller or Finance Director.
drudgery: Rebuilding similar cost calculations for each request.
Finding the latest rates, templates and allocation rules.
Explaining the same budget mechanics repeatedly.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are collecting assumptions and reconciling spreadsheet versions; this workflow needs confirmation with the analysts.

lenses.faster: Reuse a checked cost model that loads AFAS actuals and approved rates. First calculations and a source-linked explanation arrive together.
lenses.autonomous: A complete costing request triggers calculations, missing-input checks and a draft response. The analyst approves the advice before it reaches the manager.
lenses.ambitious: Give managers a costed comparison of staffing, shift and capacity options before they commit to a plan.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet rebuilding and rate hunting. Keep the conversations where the analyst helps managers understand trade-offs.
lenses.options: Compare permanent recruitment, agency cover, overtime and revised shift coverage using assumptions approved by HR and Operations.
lenses.altitude: Own the costing rules, allocation policy and quality of advice across all three sites.
reach: Prepare routine cost-allocation analysis for the Controller.
Support HR with aggregate workforce cost scenarios without setting employment terms.

tasks.human_edge: Managers need advice that reflects operational constraints and trust. The analyst challenges weak assumptions and explains who bears shared costs.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic calculations produce the numbers, while an LLM drafts explanations from approved inputs; the analyst approves the advice.

in_practice.trigger: A manager submits a standard costing request in a controlled Microsoft 365 intake.
steps: Validate the request and retrieve the latest reconciled actuals, approved rate table and allocation policy.
Calculate costs in a versioned Excel model, including employer costs, shift allowances and agency fees where applicable.
Run completeness, reconciliation and sensitivity checks; stop when required inputs or approved rules are missing.
Draft advice that separates calculated results, assumptions and unresolved questions, with links to sources.
Present the package to the analyst for approval and retain the approved version.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves advice; HR validates CAO and employment-cost assumptions, and the Controller approves allocation-policy changes.
data_needed: Actual costs by site, cost centre and account
Approved budgets and allocation keys
Applicable CAO rates, employer costs and effective dates validated by HR
Agency contracts and rate cards
Manager assumptions and operating constraints
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint costing register containing input versions, calculations, exceptions and approval.

evidence.claim: Excel Power Query can import and transform recurring structured inputs for reusable costing workbooks.
A gated costing and advice workflow could reduce end-to-end task time by 50%; this is an untested estimate for Noordhaven.

risks: Outdated CAO rates or omitted shift allowances make a precise-looking model wrong.
An allocation key can move costs between sites without improving total company performance.
Draft advice may describe an assumption as a confirmed fact.
Employee-level payroll information could be exposed unnecessarily; use restricted aggregate inputs.
research_questions: How many requests repeat existing costing methods, and how much time do they take today?
Can AFAS provide reconciled site and cost-centre data without manual repair?
Who owns and signs off CAO assumptions, agency rates and allocation keys?

tasks.short: Review site budgets and identify trends that change the forecast.

today.trigger: The nightly extract refreshes, or a weekly or monthly forecast review approaches.
steps: Load actuals, budgets and prior forecasts into Excel and Power BI.
Compare site and department spending over time.
Investigate changes in labour, agency cover and other major cost lines.
Ask managers whether movements are timing differences or lasting changes.
Update forecast assumptions and explain the proposed changes.
drudgery: Repeating the same variance calculations every cycle.
Scanning many stable cost lines to find a few meaningful changes.
Recreating charts and commentary.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are separating price, volume and timing effects and waiting for managers to confirm causes.

lenses.faster: Calculate recurring trends and variance bridges automatically, then rank movements by materiality and likely forecast impact.
lenses.autonomous: After a successful nightly refresh, publish checked trend exceptions to the analyst's review queue. Proposed forecast changes remain drafts.
lenses.ambitious: Review emerging budget pressure weekly across all sites, with explicit forecast uncertainty and follow-up on earlier predictions.
lenses.joy: Replace repetitive scanning with investigation of the few changes that matter to managers.
lenses.options: Show base, upside and downside forecasts for uncertain agency usage, wage changes and operating volumes.
lenses.altitude: Design the forecasting drivers and measure which signals actually improve forecast accuracy.
reach: Prepare the Controller's routine variance bridges.
Help Operations assess the financial effect of capacity and staffing plans.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst distinguishes a statistical movement from a business change and tests managers' explanations against operational evidence.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: rules calculate trends and reconcile totals; an LLM drafts evidence-linked explanations, and the analyst approves forecast implications.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract passes refresh and reconciliation checks.
steps: Load actuals, budget versions and available operating drivers with their reporting cut-off dates.
Calculate trends, material variances and price-volume effects where suitable driver data exists.
Flag incomplete periods, one-off entries and unexplained movements rather than assigning unsupported causes.
Draft a ranked review pack with source links, forecast scenarios and questions for managers.
Have the analyst validate causes and approve any changes to the forecast.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves forecast recommendations; budget owners confirm operational assumptions and the Finance Director approves the official forecast.
data_needed: Actuals, budgets and historical forecast versions
Accruals, accounting calendar and period status
Aggregate paid hours, agency hours and applicable rates
Operating volumes and capacity data, if available
Confirmed explanations for previous material movements
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint forecast-change register linked to the Power BI review pack and approved forecast version.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled refresh and reusable measures for recurring actual-versus-budget analysis.
Automated trend preparation with human validation could save 65% of task time; forecast accuracy gains are unproven.

risks: Missing accruals can make apparent savings disappear at close.
Seasonality and changing cost-centre mappings can produce misleading trends.
An LLM may invent causal explanations for correlated movements.
Daily reporting can create false confidence when the underlying extract is incomplete or stale.
research_questions: Which recurring drivers explain most forecast error at each site?
Are historical forecast versions and operating volumes available at matching reporting levels?
Can the workflow beat current preparation time while matching analysts' detection of material changes?

tasks.short: Check monthly departmental spending and follow up material budget overruns.

today.trigger: Monthly management accounts become available or a manager requests a spending check.
steps: Reconcile departmental reports to AFAS general ledger totals.
Compare spending with budget, prior forecast and prior periods.
Inspect transactions and accruals behind material differences.
Discuss overruns and corrective actions with budget owners.
Record explanations and carry agreed changes into the forecast.
drudgery: Copying departmental reports into standard workbooks.
Looking up transaction details for recurring exceptions.
Chasing explanations and maintaining action lists.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are transaction tracing, incomplete commitment information and repeated follow-up with budget owners.

lenses.faster: Produce reconciled variance tables and transaction evidence automatically. The analyst starts with material exceptions and previous actions.
lenses.autonomous: Each accepted reporting refresh creates an exception queue and updates existing items. Spending restrictions and accounting changes require authorised decisions.
lenses.ambitious: Track emerging overruns during the month and distinguish recurring overspend from timing, coding errors and missing accruals.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive report assembly and transaction hunting. Keep the work of finding practical corrective actions with managers.
lenses.options: Compare the financial effect of deferring purchases, changing suppliers or revising the forecast, including operational consequences.
lenses.altitude: Own the effectiveness of expenditure controls, including whether alerts lead to useful action.
reach: Prepare coding and accrual questions for the Accountant.
Support the Controller's follow-up on expenditure-control weaknesses.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst judges materiality and helps managers control costs without damaging service, safety or required staffing.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic checks identify spending exceptions, while evidence gathering and draft follow-up span several systems and need analyst approval.

in_practice.trigger: A monthly reporting snapshot is marked ready by Accounting.
steps: Reconcile cost-centre totals to the approved general ledger snapshot and identify missing inputs.
Apply approved variance thresholds and attach supporting transactions, accruals and available commitments.
Match exceptions to previous explanations and actions to avoid repeated alerts.
Draft an expenditure-control pack with unresolved questions and possible responses.
Have the analyst approve findings and action owners; track the agreed actions through resolution.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst validates findings; budget owners authorise operating actions, and Accounting approves journals and accruals.
data_needed: General ledger transactions and reporting snapshot
Department budgets and forecast versions
Accruals and available purchase commitments
Materiality thresholds and budget ownership
Previous explanations and agreed actions
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint expenditure-exception register with transaction references, reviewer decisions and action status.

evidence.claim: Power BI can calculate recurring variance measures and provide drill-through views into supporting data.
A reconciled exception workflow could reduce task time by 65%; this depends on usable transaction and commitment data.

risks: Incomplete commitments hide spending that has not yet reached the ledger.
Excessive alerts cause budget owners to ignore material exceptions.
Poorly chosen controls encourage deferring necessary maintenance or safety spending.
Unapproved coding corrections could distort reported performance.
research_questions: What proportion of current review time goes to gathering evidence versus resolving exceptions?
Are commitments and accruals available by department before the review?
Which thresholds detect material overruns without overwhelming managers?

tasks.short: Check budget submissions for missing inputs, calculation errors and compliance with approved rules.

today.trigger: A department or site submits a budget estimate or revised forecast.
steps: Check the submission against the approved template and required supporting information.
Recalculate totals and compare assumptions with actuals and approved rates.
Check cost-centre coding, allocation methods and internal approval requirements.
Refer employment-cost questions to HR and accounting-policy questions to the Controller.
Return issues to the owner and confirm corrections before consolidation.
drudgery: Checking the same cells, formulas and mandatory fields repeatedly.
Comparing assumptions with policy documents manually.
Tracking multiple corrected versions.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are inconsistent templates, undocumented assumptions and repeated correction rounds.

lenses.faster: Run formula, completeness, coding and approved-rate checks immediately on submission. Review one consolidated issue list.
lenses.autonomous: Routine submissions pass defined validation rules automatically; exceptions go to the analyst. Passing validation does not approve the budget.
lenses.ambitious: Check every submission consistently and show where errors repeatedly enter the budget process.
lenses.joy: Remove cell-by-cell checking and version comparison. Keep judgement about unusual assumptions and material exceptions.
lenses.options: Show compliant corrections for each issue, such as an approved rate or allocation method, with their cost effects.
lenses.altitude: Maintain a versioned budget-control rulebook and improve templates based on recurring errors.
reach: Prepare evidence for the Controller's budget-control review.
Help HR maintain a finance-facing table of validated employment-cost assumptions.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst recognises when a submission passes formal checks but remains unrealistic, and escalates policy questions to the right owner.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: completeness, arithmetic, coding and approved-rate checks have explicit rules and checkable outputs; ambiguous policy questions remain exceptions.

in_practice.trigger: A budget submission is uploaded to the designated SharePoint location.
steps: Identify the template version and reject unsupported or incomplete files with a clear issue list.
Run arithmetic, account-mapping, duplicate-line and required-assumption checks.
Compare rates and allocation methods with approved rules effective for the budget period.
Route ambiguous or material exceptions to the analyst, HR or Controller and recheck corrected submissions.
Record the validation result and release technically valid submissions for separate budget approval.
in_practice.human_gate: People resolve policy exceptions and approve budgets; the software only confirms conformance with explicitly approved checks.
data_needed: Versioned budget templates and required fields
Valid account and cost-centre mappings
Approved allocation rules and approval limits
HR-validated CAO rates and employment-cost assumptions
Accounting policies and effective dates
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint validation register containing the submitted file version, rule version, failed checks and exception decisions.

evidence.claim: Excel supports data validation and formula-based checks, while Power Query can combine structured submissions.
Automating explicit budget checks could save 60% of task time; the estimate assumes reasonably standard submissions.

risks: An incomplete rulebook creates false assurance about compliance.
Rules may use the wrong effective date for CAO or policy changes.
Unusual but valid submissions may be rejected unnecessarily.
A validation pass could be mistaken for financial or legal approval.
research_questions: What share of historic review findings can be expressed as explicit rules?
How consistently do sites use the approved submission template?
Can a trial detect known errors while keeping false positives manageable?

tasks.short: Calculate the funding needed for a proposed site project or business initiative.

today.trigger: Operations or management proposes a project such as extra warehouse capacity, equipment or a process change.
steps: Clarify the scope, timing and operating assumptions with the project owner.
Gather comparable actual costs, supplier estimates and staffing assumptions.
Build an Excel model covering investment, operating costs, working capital and cash timing.
Test uncertain assumptions and identify missing costs.
Review the funding requirement with the Controller and project owner.
drudgery: Searching historical projects for comparable costs.
Transcribing quotes and assumptions into models.
Rebuilding cash-flow and sensitivity schedules.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are incomplete project scope, scattered estimates and repeated changes to timing or staffing assumptions.

lenses.faster: Populate a standard project model from reconciled historical costs and reviewed quote extractions. Calculate cash timing and sensitivities automatically.
lenses.autonomous: A project intake triggers a draft funding model and a missing-information list. New evidence produces a versioned recalculation for review.
lenses.ambitious: Cost smaller operational improvements that currently receive little analysis, then compare their realised costs and benefits with the original case.
lenses.joy: Remove document searching and model setup. Keep the investigative work of finding overlooked costs and testing feasibility.
lenses.options: Compare phased delivery, lease versus purchase and alternative start dates using consistent cash and operating assumptions.
lenses.altitude: Own the company's project-costing method and the feedback loop from delivered projects to future estimates.
reach: Prepare project cash schedules for the Controller's liquidity planning.
Support Operations with financial comparisons of supplier and delivery options.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst challenges scope, validates operational feasibility and recognises costs or dependencies that historical records do not capture.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: gathering project evidence and extracting estimates require several steps; deterministic models calculate funding and a person validates the case.

in_practice.trigger: A project owner submits a defined scope and initial delivery assumptions.
steps: Retrieve approved comparable costs and extract quote details into a structured evidence table.
Flag missing scope, expired quotes and assumptions requiring confirmation.
Calculate investment, operating costs, working capital, contingency and cash timing using approved model rules.
Generate scenarios and a funding summary with sources and explicit uncertainty.
Have the analyst and project owner validate the model before funding approval.
in_practice.human_gate: The project owner confirms scope; the analyst validates the estimate, the Controller checks accounting treatment, and the authorised manager approves funding.
data_needed: Project scope, delivery schedule and operating assumptions
Historical project costs with comparable scope
Supplier quotes and payment terms
HR-validated staffing and training cost assumptions
Approved capitalisation, VAT, discount-rate and contingency policies
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint project-case folder with source documents, model versions, assumption owners and approvals.

evidence.claim: Excel supports discounted cash-flow calculations and scenario analysis for project funding models.
Combining evidence extraction with standard project models could save 55% of task time; novel projects may save much less.

risks: Historical comparisons may omit differences in capacity, site conditions or implementation scope.
Quote extraction can confuse totals, VAT, recurring charges or payment dates.
Unsupported benefits can make an unattractive project appear viable.
Workforce changes may require HR review and applicable works council procedures before implementation.
research_questions: Are historical project costs and outcomes stored with enough scope detail to support comparisons?
Which omitted costs have caused previous projects to exceed their budgets?
Can a pilot reproduce an approved business case and its cash timing within agreed tolerances?

tasks.short: Summarise funding requests and recommend which ones management should approve.

today.trigger: A budget owner requests new funding or a change to an approved spending envelope.
steps: Collect the request, business case and relevant budget position.
Check affordability, expected benefits, timing and approval authority.
Compare the request with competing demands and available funding.
Write a recommendation, including conditions or reasons to decline.
Submit the decision pack and record management's decision.
drudgery: Reformatting business cases into approval papers.
Repeating affordability calculations.
Finding missing attachments and tracking decision status.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are incomplete requests, inconsistent benefit claims and clarification rounds before an approver can decide.

lenses.faster: Generate a consistent decision pack from validated models, current budget headroom and the approval matrix.
lenses.autonomous: A complete request triggers affordability checks and a draft recommendation. The analyst approves the recommendation before submission.
lenses.ambitious: Assess requests together as a portfolio, showing cash constraints, operational dependencies and displaced priorities.
lenses.joy: Remove paper assembly and repeated calculations. Keep the judgement about whether a request deserves scarce funding.
lenses.options: Present approve, phase, reduce scope, defer and decline options with comparable financial effects.
lenses.altitude: Design decision criteria and check whether funded proposals deliver the benefits used to justify them.
reach: Prepare the Finance Director's investment and funding review materials.
Help the Controller maintain a consistent funding-decision register.

tasks.human_edge: Funding choices involve strategy, service reliability and competing interests. The analyst must challenge benefit claims and make a defensible recommendation.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: the workflow assembles evidence and drafts recommendations, but financial judgement and funding authority remain explicit human gates.

in_practice.trigger: A funding request has a named owner, completed model and required supporting evidence.
steps: Validate completeness, approval authority and links to the underlying cost model.
Calculate budget headroom and cash effects, accounting for existing approved commitments.
Compare feasible options against approved financial and operational criteria.
Draft a recommendation that separates verified evidence, assumptions and judgement.
Have the analyst approve the pack, route it to the authorised decision maker and record the decision.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst owns the recommendation; only the manager specified in the approval matrix can approve funding.
data_needed: Validated request model and evidence
Current budget headroom and approved commitments
Cash forecast and funding constraints
Approval matrix and investment criteria
Competing requests and project dependencies
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint funding register with recommendation versions, approver identity, decision, conditions and supporting evidence.

evidence.claim: SharePoint lists and document libraries can hold structured request records and versioned approval documents.
Automated preparation and gated recommendations could save 60% of task time; strategic deliberation remains human work.

risks: A convincing draft may conceal weak evidence or uncertain benefits.
Stale commitment data can overstate available funding.
A scoring model can undervalue safety, compliance or service resilience.
Workflow routing could be mistaken for approval or exceed delegated authority.
research_questions: How much time is spent assembling packs versus deciding what to recommend?
Are commitments and the approval matrix reliable enough for automatic affordability checks?
Would retrospective packs preserve the key concerns raised in previous funding decisions?

tasks.short: Organise regular budget reports and coordinate special analysis requests.

today.trigger: The reporting calendar reaches a deadline or management requests a special budget report.
steps: Agree the purpose, audience, scope and deadline.
Assign inputs and confirm when Accounting's numbers will be ready.
Collect data and commentary from Finance and site managers.
Assemble the report and check totals, versions and explanations.
Resolve gaps and release the approved report to its audience.
drudgery: Chasing inputs and checking whether they are current.
Copying tables and charts between tools.
Maintaining separate versions of the same report.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are late commentary, changing report specifications and rework when ledger figures move during close.

lenses.faster: Build recurring packs from one reconciled reporting model and reuse approved report specifications.
lenses.autonomous: The reporting calendar starts preparation and tracks missing inputs. An approved workflow can send reminders; the analyst controls report release.
lenses.ambitious: Provide concise site and company reports tailored to the decisions each audience must make, with direct access to supporting figures.
lenses.joy: Reduce chasing, copying and formatting. Keep editorial judgement and conversations about what management needs to know.
lenses.options: Produce an executive summary, a site view and a detailed finance appendix from the same approved snapshot.
lenses.altitude: Own the reporting service: definitions, deadlines, quality checks and whether reports help decisions.
reach: Coordinate the Controller's management-reporting timetable.
Prepare first drafts of Finance Director presentation materials.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst negotiates priorities, resolves conflicting explanations and decides which messages deserve management attention.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: report preparation crosses data, documents and contributors; automated assembly needs a person to resolve gaps and approve release.

in_practice.trigger: A reporting-calendar milestone or an accepted special-report brief starts the workflow.
steps: Load the approved report specification, audience permissions and input deadlines.
Check extract freshness, reconciliation status and readiness of required commentary.
Assemble tables, charts and draft narrative from a fixed reporting snapshot.
Flag conflicting explanations, late inputs and changes since the previous version.
Have the analyst approve content and distribution, then archive the released snapshot and pack.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves content and recipients; the Controller confirms close status and the Finance Director signs off board-level material where required.
data_needed: Reporting calendar and report specifications
Approved financial snapshot and metric definitions
Named input owners and approved commentary
Audience permissions and distribution lists
Previous released packs and outstanding actions
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint reporting register recording source snapshot, contributors, checks, approval and released version.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports reusable reports, refresh schedules and export of report content to PowerPoint.
Automated assembly and input tracking could save 55% of task time; coordinating people and special requests will remain substantial.

risks: Different refresh times can leave tables and commentary describing different snapshots.
Automated narrative may overstate confidence in provisional close figures.
Incorrect audience permissions could expose payroll or commercially sensitive information.
Generating more reports can consume management attention without improving decisions.
research_questions: Which recurring reports lead to decisions, and which are rarely used?
How much preparation time is copying and formatting versus coordination and review?
Can every released figure and explanation be traced to the same approved snapshot?

tasks.short: Reconcile project budgets with site and company funding envelopes, including contingency.

today.trigger: Budgets are consolidated, funding is transferred or contingency use is requested; public-sector appropriations translate here to internal funding envelopes.
steps: Collect approved project, department, site and company budget versions.
Map detailed budgets to their parent funding envelopes.
Check that allocations, approved transfers and remaining balances reconcile.
Separate contingency reserves from committed and spent amounts.
Investigate mismatches and submit proposed corrections or transfers for approval.
drudgery: Matching spreadsheet lines to parent budgets.
Checking totals after every transfer or version change.
Tracking contingency releases across separate records.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are inconsistent project identifiers, overlapping budget versions and transfers recorded in only one place.

lenses.faster: Use a controlled budget hierarchy and transfer register to reconcile parent and child balances automatically.
lenses.autonomous: Every approved budget version or transfer triggers reconciliation. Only unresolved mappings and balance breaks reach the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a clear view of allocated, committed, spent and available funding across all three sites, with contingency shown separately.
lenses.joy: Remove manual matching and repeated summation. Keep investigation of genuine funding conflicts.
lenses.options: Simulate alternative reallocations or contingency releases without changing the approved funding baseline.
lenses.altitude: Own the budget hierarchy and transfer controls that prevent double allocation and hidden reserve use.
reach: Support the Controller's budget-governance controls.
Provide reconciled funding availability for project owners and cash-planning discussions.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst resolves ambiguous ownership and judges whether a proposed transfer respects the purpose and conditions of approved funding.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: hierarchy mapping, balance reconciliation and transfer checks are explicit calculations; people approve changes to funding authority.

in_practice.trigger: An approved budget version or authorised transfer enters the controlled register.
steps: Validate unique identifiers, parent mappings, approval references and effective dates.
Recalculate parent-child balances using one documented treatment of commitments and actual spending.
Check duplicate allocations, unauthorised transfers, reserve releases and negative available balances.
Publish reconciled balances and route exceptions to the analyst with supporting records.
Apply approved corrections and retain the complete version and transfer history.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst resolves mapping exceptions; the authorised budget owner or Finance Director approves transfers and contingency releases before they affect official balances.
data_needed: Approved budget hierarchy and unique project identifiers
Budget versions and parent funding limits
Authorised transfers and contingency releases
Actual spending and commitments with clear overlap rules
Funding conditions and approval limits
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint budget-control register containing reconciliations, exceptions, transfer approvals and version history.

evidence.claim: Power Query can merge budget tables, group amounts by hierarchy and identify unmatched records.
A stable hierarchy and controlled transfer register could reduce reconciliation time by 70%; actual savings depend on identifier quality.

risks: Actuals and commitments may be double counted when calculating available funding.
A wrong parent mapping can reconcile mathematically while assigning money to the wrong purpose.
Contingency may be counted both centrally and within project budgets.
Automatic reconciliation must not create authority to transfer or spend funds.
research_questions: Does Noordhaven actually maintain nested project envelopes and contingency reserves, and at what scale?
Are project identifiers and approved transfers consistent across AFAS and budget workbooks?
Can the proposed balance rules reproduce current approved funding availability without double counting?

role.altitude: The FP&A Analyst becomes the owner of financial decision models, forecast assumptions and exception review across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Routine preparation runs through controlled workflows; the analyst spends more time testing explanations and helping managers act.
reach: Prepare more of the Controller's variance analysis, reporting controls and budget reconciliations.
Support the Finance Director with funding portfolios, cash scenarios and decision packs.
Help Operations compare capacity, agency staffing and project options.
Partner with HR on aggregate workforce costing using HR-approved CAO and employment assumptions.
Work with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst on consistent workforce definitions and restricted data access.
role.ceiling_note: These tasks cover about 1,134 hours per FTE annually. The illustrative savings total roughly 1,350 hours across both analysts, worth about EUR 108,000 of annual capacity at EUR 80/hour before implementation, maintenance and review costs; they are not a headcount-saving commitment. Benefits depend on reconciled extracts, stable identifiers and available operating drivers. Spending authority, accounting sign-off and operational judgement remain with people.
skills_to_grow: Build and maintain Excel Power Query models and Power BI measures with reconciliation controls.
Design driver-based forecasts, uncertainty ranges and useful scenario comparisons.
Maintain versioned assumptions, budget hierarchies and approval rules.
Evaluate LLM drafts for unsupported claims and preserve source traceability.
Challenge business cases and explain financial trade-offs to site managers.
Apply AVG/GDPR access and retention controls to payroll-derived information.
Recognise when workforce proposals require HR, works council or legal involvement.
role.ambitious_version: Run a weekly financial outlook that connects reconciled actuals, staffing costs, available operating volumes and project commitments. Show management emerging pressure, credible options and uncertainty before month-end, then measure forecast accuracy and realised project benefits. Pilot each workflow against current results and track days to close, preparation time, reviewer corrections and audit adjustments. Use aggregate workforce data for financial planning; any expansion into individual employment decisions requires a separate assessment of AVG/GDPR, applicable EU AI Act obligations and works council rights.
